# one place rather than being duplicated across generated hook commands.

# hooks emit JSON there).
log() {
	printf '[entire-dev] %s\n' "$1" >&2
}

# regardless of the caller's working directory. Parameter expansion avoids
# depending on external tools like dirname, which may not be on PATH when this
# runs from a minimal hook environment.

esac
root=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$script_dir/.." && pwd)

# split across multiple files (e.g. the git-remote-entire dispatch in
# remotehelper.go), and naming a single file would leave the others out and
# fail to compile.
pkg="$root/cmd/entire"

# "entire clean" may remove .entire/tmp/, which just costs one rebuild.
# Concurrent hook invocations can race the rebuild of a stale binary; a
# failed build here simply falls through to the PATH binary.
bin="$root/.entire/tmp/entire-dev-bin"
if command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1 &&
	mkdir -p "${bin%/*}" 2>/dev/null &&
	go build -o "$bin" "$pkg" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	exec "$bin" "$@"
fi

# binary so hooks keep working while the source is broken.
if command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	log "project isn't compiling; falling back to the entire binary on PATH"
	exec entire "$@"
fi

log "project isn't compiling and no entire binary on PATH; skipping hook"

**Mostly, yes — with two honest caveats.** The fix caches the local-dev binary in `.entire/tmp/` so `go build` skips the link when nothing changed: the measured session-end round trip dropped from 1.66s to **0.91s**, under Claude Code's ~1.5s SessionEnd budget. The caveats:

- My 0.91s measurement was a no-op session. A real session-end also runs the **eager condense**, which can add seconds when there's pending checkpoint work. That's the part suggestion #2 addresses.
- Claude Code has an upstream regression (since v2.1.72) where **Ctrl-C exits cancel SessionEnd hooks immediately** regardless of speed. Nothing we do client-side guarantees survival there; `/exit`-style exits should be fine.

## 2. Is the self-healing manual?

The **sweep** (`finalizeExitedSessions`) runs only inside `entire status`, `entire status --json`, and `entire doctor` — so that specific mechanism is triggered by commands, yes. But the part that actually matters for your data is fully automatic: pending checkpoint work is **condensed to `entire/checkpoints/v1` on your next commit via the post-commit git hook**, whether or not session-end ever ran (the session-end condense is just an eager version of the same thing, explicitly documented as fail-open). What the sweep adds is bookkeeping — marking dead sessions ENDED so they stop showing as "active" in listings. Without it they just linger cosmetically (there's also a 1-hour `StuckActiveThreshold` for liveness classification). So: **no checkpoint data is ever lost by the cancelled hook.**

content.text:
Good questions — let me take them one at a time, because "just raise the timeout" is the tempting fix and it's only half true.

## Is the timeout the issue?

The per-hook `"timeout"` field (seconds) exists and applies to SessionEnd, so raising it is worth doing — but it's a mitigation, not the root cause, for two reasons:

1. **Claude Code doesn't block exit on SessionEnd hooks.** SessionEnd has no decision control; it's fire-and-forget teardown. The GitHub reports ([#41577](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/41577), [#32712](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/32712)) show hooks being killed at exit *even with a generous configured timeout* — on Ctrl-C the cancel is immediate and ignores the timeout entirely. So a raised timeout helps the polite `/exit` path, but doesn't make a slow hook safe.
2. **Our hook was pathologically slow for no reason.** It paid a full Go link (~1.3s) on every single invocation even when nothing changed, because `go build -o /dev/null` can never be "up to date". That's fixed now regardless of what the timeout is — a hook that finishes in under a second wins under any cancellation policy that gives it *any* window.

So: timeout raise = belt and suspenders on top of the speed fix, not a substitute. I'll add it to the SessionEnd entry on this branch since it's cheap.

## "Don't we just have to track when the session ends?"

Yes — you've independently arrived at exactly what suggestion #2 is. The *essential* work at SessionEnd is tiny: flip the session state to ENDED (a small file write, milliseconds). Everything else the handler does — the eager condense — is an optimization that already has automatic fallbacks (PostCommit retries it on your next commit; the sweep retries it too). The only reason the condense runs eagerly at session end is issue #591 (zombie ENDED sessions piling up condense debt that made every future commit slower), so "just mark it and defer the rest" is a real design change that needs to not regress that — either defer to the existing retry paths, or detach the condense into a background process that survives the hook being cancelled. That's why I'd keep it as its own PR.

One correction to the framing though: before today's fix, even "just track the end" would have failed — the launcher couldn't get a Go process *started* inside the budget. So the ordering is: #1 (shipped) makes the hook reach the handler at all; #2 makes the handler's work fit any budget; the timeout raise buys margin.

192	func waitForTranscriptFlush(ctx context.Context, transcriptPath string, hookStartTime time.Time) {
193		const (
194			maxWait      = 3 * time.Second
195			pollInterval = 50 * time.Millisecond
196			tailBytes    = 4096
197			maxSkew      = 2 * time.Second
198		)
199	
200		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "agent.claudecode")
201	
202		// Fast path: skip the poll loop when the sentinel can't possibly appear.
203		// - File doesn't exist: nothing to poll.
204		// - File is stale (unmodified for 2+ min): agent isn't running anymore.
205		//   This avoids 3s timeouts per stale "active" session (e.g., agent crashed
206		//   without firing stop hook).
207		const staleThreshold = 2 * time.Minute
208		info, err := os.Stat(transcriptPath)
209		if err != nil {
210			// Most likely the file doesn't exist; other errors (permission, etc.)
211			// would also prevent polling, so skip the wait either way.
212			return
213		}
214		fileAge := time.Since(info.ModTime())
215		if fileAge > staleThreshold {
216			logging.Debug(logCtx, "transcript file is stale, skipping sentinel wait",
217				slog.Duration("file_age", fileAge),
218			)
219			return
220		}
221	
222		deadline := time.Now().Add(maxWait)
223		for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
224			if checkStopSentinel(transcriptPath, tailBytes, hookStartTime, maxSkew) {
225				logging.Debug(logCtx, "transcript flush sentinel found",
226					slog.Duration("wait", time.Since(hookStartTime)),
227				)

229			}
230			time.Sleep(pollInterval)
231		}
232		logging.Warn(logCtx, "transcript flush sentinel not found within timeout, proceeding",
233			slog.Duration("timeout", maxWait),
234		)

content.content:
{"body":"## Summary

Orphaned sessions accumulate silently and cause severe performance degradation:
- **RAM**: `entire hooks claude-code stop` processes consuming 1.7GB+ each (two concurrent = 3.4GB)
- **Commit speed**: `entire hooks git post-commit` takes **2 minutes 44 seconds** per commit (synchronous, blocking)
- **Session accumulation**: 76 orphaned sessions accumulated over 18 days without any warning

## Impact

This went unnoticed for weeks. Real cost:
- Every git commit blocked for ~3 minutes
- With 6 commits per session, that is ~16 minutes of dead time per session
- Two concurrent session stops consumed 3.4GB RAM on a dev laptop
- `entire status` showed 60+ "active" sessions that were actually dead

## Root Cause

Sessions from Claude Code subagents (spawned via Agent tool) are not properly cleaned up when the parent session ends. These zombie sessions remain in Entire's state and are re-processed on every commit hook and session stop.

The condensation pipeline loads full JSONL transcripts into memory. With large transcripts (up to 15MB each) and 76 sessions to process, memory balloons.

## Reproduction

1. Use Claude Code with frequent subagent spawning over several days
2. Run `entire status` - observe dozens of "active" sessions from days/weeks ago
3. Make a git commit - observe multi-minute blocking
4. Check RAM: `ps aux | grep entire` shows 1.5GB+ per process

## Workaround

```bash
# Fix stuck sessions (needs ACCESSIBLE=1 for non-interactive use)
ACCESSIBLE=1 entire doctor

# Clean orphaned sessions
entire clean --force

# Verify
entire status
```

This brought my session count from 60+ down to 12, and commit times back to normal.

## Suggestions

1. **Auto-cleanup**: Expire sessions that have been idle for >24h (or configurable threshold)
2. **Memory cap**: Stream/chunk transcript processing instead of loading full JSONL into memory
3. **Async post-commit**: The `post-commit` hook should run in the background. A 2m44s synchronous hook on every commit is not acceptable
4. **Visibility**: Warn when orphaned session count exceeds a threshold (e.g. >10)
5. **Subagent awareness**: Detect when a Claude Code session spawns subagents and auto-close their Entire sessions when the parent ends

## Environment

- Entire CLI: `entire version` (installed via Homebrew)
- OS: macOS 15.4 (Apple Silicon)
- Agent: Claude Code (Opus 4.6)
- Strategy: `manual-commit`
- Repo transcript count: 374 JSONL files, 323MB total
- Largest single transcript: 15MB","title":"Orphaned sessions cause 3GB+ RAM usage and 2m44s commit times"}

content.text: `execx.SpawnDetached` already exists and is even test-aware. Let me see its contract and who uses it today:

content.content:
1	package execx
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"io"
6		"os"
7		"os/exec"
8		"testing"
9	)
10	
11	// SpawnDetached re-execs the current executable as a detached, fire-and-forget
12	// child running args, surviving the parent's exit (new session on Unix,
13	// CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP | DETACHED_PROCESS on Windows, via detachFromTTY).
14	// The child runs in dir (os.TempDir() when empty, so the child never holds the
15	// parent's working directory), inherits the parent's environment, and has its
16	// stdout/stderr discarded. Best-effort: every error is swallowed — callers
17	// treat the spawn as advisory background work.
18	//
19	// In-process `go test` runs are a no-op: the current executable is the test
20	// binary, and re-execing it would fork the whole suite. Tests exercise the
21	// call sites through their spawn seams instead.
22	func SpawnDetached(dir string, args ...string) {
23		if testing.Testing() {
24			return
25		}
26		executable, err := os.Executable()
27		if err != nil {
28			return
29		}
30	
31		// context.Background(): the child must outlive the parent, so it is never
32		// tied to a cancellable context.
33		cmd := exec.CommandContext(context.Background(), executable, args...)
34		detachFromTTY(cmd)
35		cmd.Dir = dir
36		if cmd.Dir == "" {
37			cmd.Dir = os.TempDir()
38		}
39		cmd.Env = os.Environ()
40		cmd.Stdout = io.Discard
41		cmd.Stderr = io.Discard
42	
43		if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
44			return
45		}
46		// Release the process so it can run independently of the parent.
47		//nolint:errcheck // best effort — the child continues regardless
48		_ = cmd.Process.Release()
49	}

content.text:
Here's the full picture in plain terms:

## The problem shape

When you exit Claude Code, it fires the SessionEnd hook but gives it ~1.5 seconds and won't wait longer — it's fire-and-forget teardown. Our hook was doing two jobs in that window:

1. **Mark the session ENDED** — a locked state-file write, takes milliseconds
2. **Eagerly condense** the session's pending checkpoints to the permanent `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch — transcript reads + git tree building, takes seconds

Job 2 can never reliably fit the budget, no matter how fast the launcher is. So the hook gets killed mid-work, you see "Hook cancelled," and neither job completes — the session isn't even *marked* ended.

## The pattern (which already exists in this codebase)

The CLI already solved this exact problem twice: `__send_analytics` and `__refresh_trail_enablement` are hidden commands that get spawned via `execx.SpawnDetached` — the parent re-execs itself as a detached child (`setsid`, new process group) and returns immediately. The child **survives the parent being killed**, because Claude Code kills the hook's process group, and the detached child isn't in it.

So the fix is to split the two jobs along their natural line:

```
SessionEnd hook (must be fast)          Detached child (can take as long as it needs)
─────────────────────────────          ──────────────────────────────────────────────
markSessionEnded()   ~ms      ──spawn──▶  entire __condense_session <id>
return 0 immediately                        └─ CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed()
```

The mark stays in the hook because it needs the hook's event payload (model name, turn counts). The condense moves out because it's slow and needs nothing from the hook but the session ID. Nothing about *what* happens changes — same eager condensation, same #591 protection — only *where* it executes.

## Why it's safe

- `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` is already fail-open, idempotent-ish, and guarded (skips sessions with pending `FilesTouched`, re-checks state under lock) — it was designed to be retried from multiple places (PostCommit, the status/doctor sweep), so a third caller is not a new race class.
- If the detached child dies (laptop lid closes), the existing retry paths pick it up — that's the self-healing we discussed.

## What I was doing when you interrupted

The last piece: integration tests spawn the real binary, so the detach would actually fork there and make ~every session-end test racy. The plan was one line in the integration `TestMain` — set `ENTIRE_SESSION_END_SYNC=1` process-wide so all existing tests keep the deterministic inline behavior — plus one new test that opts out and exercises the real detached flow with polling.

State right now: the split handler, the `__condense_session` command, and five unit tests are written and green. Remaining: the TestMain line, the detached-flow integration test, full test suite + lint, commit. Want me to finish that?

content.text:
Checkpoint refs are covered — and verifying that was worth it. Here's the precise picture:

**Condensation doesn't write "the v1 branch" directly — it writes through a backend-agnostic store.** The condense path calls `getPersistentStore` → `checkpoint.Open`, which reads the repo's checkpoints config, resolves the configured **primary backend** (git-branch → `entire/checkpoints/v1`, or git-refs → per-checkpoint refs under `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>`), builds any **mirrors**, and wraps them in a fanout store. My "v1 branch" phrasing earlier was legacy shorthand; on a refs-primary repo the eager condense writes per-checkpoint refs (and deliberately never seeds a vestigial v1 branch).

**Why the detach doesn't disturb any of this:** the detached child runs the *identical* `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` function the hook used to run inline — same store resolution, same fanout, same push-discovery bookkeeping downstream. The only variable that could have changed is *where the config resolves from*, because `settings.LoadCheckpointsConfig` is worktree-relative. That's exactly why `SpawnDetached(worktreeRoot, ...)` sets the child's working directory to the worktree root — the child resolves the same repo, same settings, same backend as the inline call would have. (Same reason the existing `__refresh_trail_enablement` child is spawned with the worktree root.)

So the invariant across backends is: **nothing about what gets written or where changes — only which process does the writing.** Branch-primary repos, refs-primary repos, and mid-migration repos that read both formats all behave identically; the mirror fanout and the pre-push mirror ingestion path (the one from the neolime finding — refs only reach the web through the `entire://` mirror push) are downstream of condense and untouched.

Here's everything, annotated:

## 1. The proof — a real Claude session that exited through the fix

The session I ran headlessly in the worktree (`claude -p "Reply with exactly: ok"`), its actual record:

```json
{
    "session_id": "67bacf06-...",
    "started_at": "2026-07-23T16:32:33",
    "ended_at":   "2026-07-23T16:32:42",   ← stamped at the real exit (9.6s session)
    "phase": "ended",                       ← marked inside the hook, in milliseconds
    "fully_condensed": true,                ← landed by the detached __condense_session child
    "last_prompt": "Reply with exactly: ok",
    "session_turn_count": 1
}
```

Contrast with your 45-hour zombie, which is what **every** session in this repo has looked like since May 29:

```json
{
    "session_id": "d5a74b46-...",
    "started_at": "2026-07-21T11:52:52",
    "ended_at":   null,                     ← hook cancelled on every exit
    "phase": "idle",                        ← never closed, invisible to the sweep
    "fully_condensed": null
}
```

## 2. The numbers

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Warm session-end hook | 1.66s+ (over the ~1.5s budget → cancelled) | **0.99s** |
| Launcher overhead per hook | full Go link every time (~1.3s) | cached binary, ~0.4s staleness check |
| Condense location | inline in the hook (killed mid-work) | detached child, survives hook cancellation |

## 3. The change itself — two commits, 381 lines

```
fc0d33824  fix(entire-dev): cache the local-dev binary so hooks fit SessionEnd's budget
540f83e09  fix(lifecycle): detach the session-end condense so the ENDED mark survives hook cancellation

 scripts/entire-dev                       |  38 ++++--   ← cached binary instead of go run
 cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go              |  30 ++++-   ← hook: mark inline, spawn condense
 cmd/entire/cli/session_end_condense.go   |  72 +++++    ← hidden __condense_session command
 cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint_policy_warning.go |  2 +-
 cmd/entire/cli/root.go                   |   1 +
 + 3 test files (unit seam tests, detached-flow integration test, TestMain sync env)
```

And the heart of it, the new hook flow in `handleLifecycleSessionEnd`:

```go
// Agents give SessionEnd hooks a short budget and never wait for them on
// exit (Claude Code cancels after ~1.5s), so only the fast ENDED mark runs
// inline; the eager condense — transcript reads plus git tree building —
// is handed to a detached child that survives the hook being killed.
ended, err := markSessionEnded(ctx, event, event.SessionID, nil)   // milliseconds
...
if ended {
    sessionEndCondenseSpawn(worktreeRoot, event.SessionID)          // fire-and-forget
}
```

gh pr create --title "fix: SessionEnd hooks were cancelled on every exit — sessions never marked ended" --body "## Why

Claude Code gives SessionEnd hooks a short budget (~1.5s) and never waits for them on exit. Our hook blew that budget two ways at once, so **every session exit since 2026-05-29 printed \`SessionEnd hook failed: Hook cancelled\` and no session was ever marked ended**:

- \`.entire\` logs: 117 successful \`session-end\` events Feb–May, zero after May 29
- Real sessions sat \`idle\` with \`ended_at: null\` for days (e.g. the \"45 hours\" / \"177 hours\" durations on entire.io session pages), then got silently deleted by the 7-day stale sweep without ever reporting an end
- Timing lined up with 0ef509db (2026-05-27), which added a \`go build -o /dev/null\` probe to \`scripts/entire-dev\` — that output path defeats go's up-to-date short-circuit, forcing a **full link on every hook invocation** (~1.3s warm) before \`go run\` linked again

## What

**Commit 1 — \`scripts/entire-dev\`: cache the local-dev binary.** Build into \`.entire/tmp/entire-dev-bin\` (ignored via the committed \`.entire/.gitignore\`) and exec it. An up-to-date tree costs one staleness check (~0.4s) instead of two links; the fake session-end round trip drops 1.66s → 0.91s. Stop/turn-end hooks re-warm the cache during the session, so SessionEnd almost always hits the warm path. Fallback semantics unchanged: broken tree → PATH binary → exit 0.

**Commit 2 — lifecycle: split the SessionEnd handler along its natural line.** The ENDED mark (a locked state-file write carrying hook event metadata, milliseconds) stays inline; the eager condense (transcript reads + git tree building, seconds) moves to a detached \`__condense_session\` child spawned via \`execx.SpawnDetached\` — the existing \`__refresh_trail_enablement\` pattern — which survives the hook process being killed.

The condense itself is unchanged: same \`CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed\`, same fail-open + retry semantics (PostCommit / exited-session sweep), same backend routing (git-branch or git-refs primary + mirrors), run from the worktree root so config resolution matches the inline call. The #591 protection (eager condense on end) is preserved — just relocated. The sweep keeps its synchronous condense.

\`ENTIRE_SESSION_END_SYNC\` forces the old inline sequence; the integration TestMain sets it process-wide so existing session-end assertions stay deterministic, and a dedicated integration test exercises the real detached flow by overriding it back to empty.

## Verification

- 8,306 unit / 438 integration (incl. #591 regression test) / 63 e2e canary — all green
- Live end-to-end: real headless Claude session in the worktree → no warning, \`phase: ended\`, real \`ended_at\`, \`fully_condensed: true\` via the detached child — the first real session-end to complete in this repo since May 29
- Interactive end-to-end: fresh \`claude\` session, \`/exit\` → clean exit (no cancelled-hook warning), session marked ended at the actual exit moment; condense correctly deferred to commit-time because the session had touched files

## Notes / follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Ctrl-C double-tap force-quit still cancels SessionEnd hooks regardless of speed — upstream Claude Code regression (anthropics/claude-code#32712)
- Crash/kill paths (no hook fires) leave IDLE sessions the sweep is blind to (\`OwnerExited\` is ACTIVE-only) and the 7-day stale cleanup deletes them silently instead of finalizing — worth a separate issue
- Session \"duration\" on entire.io is wall-clock span (start → last activity); this fix makes \`ended_at\` real but doesn't change that metric's definition

+//go:build integration
+
+package integration
+
+import (
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/session"
+)
+
+// TestSessionEnd_DetachedCondense exercises the production SessionEnd flow:
+// the hook marks the session ENDED inline (fast enough for agents' short
+// SessionEnd budgets — Claude Code cancels the hook after ~1.5s) and hands
+// the eager condense to a detached __condense_session child that survives
+// the hook process being killed. The ENDED mark must be observable as soon
+// as the hook returns; the condense lands asynchronously.
+func TestSessionEnd_DetachedCondense(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
+	sess := env.NewSession()
+
+	if err := env.SimulateUserPromptSubmit(sess.ID); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("SimulateUserPromptSubmit failed: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	env.WriteFile("detached.go", "package main\n\nfunc Detached() {}\n")
+	sess.CreateTranscript("Create detached.go", []FileChange{
+		{Path: "detached.go", Content: "package main\n\nfunc Detached() {}\n"},
+	})
+
+	// Commit the file BEFORE stopping so FilesTouched is empty at session end
+	// and the eager condense actually runs (sessions with FilesTouched defer
+	// to PostCommit for carry-forward tracking).
+	env.GitAdd("detached.go")
+	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add detached.go", "detached.go")
+
+	if err := env.SimulateStop(sess.ID, sess.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("SimulateStop failed: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	if err := env.SimulateSessionEndDetached(sess.ID); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("SimulateSessionEndDetached failed: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	// The ENDED mark is synchronous — it must hold the moment the hook returns.
+	state, err := env.GetSessionState(sess.ID)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("GetSessionState failed: %v", err)
+	}
+	if state == nil {
+		t.Fatal("session state missing after session-end")
+	}
+	if state.Phase != session.PhaseEnded {
+		t.Fatalf("phase = %s immediately after session-end, want ended", state.Phase)
+	}
+	if state.EndedAt == nil {
+		t.Fatal("EndedAt should be set immediately after session-end")
+	}
+
+	// The condense is detached — poll until the child lands it.
+	deadline := time.Now().Add(15 * time.Second)
+	for {
+		state, err = env.GetSessionState(sess.ID)
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("GetSessionState failed while polling: %v", err)
+		}
+		if state != nil && state.FullyCondensed {
+			break
+		}
+		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
+			t.Fatalf("detached condense did not mark session FullyCondensed within 15s (phase=%s)", state.Phase)
+		}
+		time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
+	}
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+package cli
+
+import (
+	"log/slog"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/execx"
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
+
+	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
+)
+
+// envSessionEndSyncCondense forces the SessionEnd hook to run the eager
+// condense inline instead of handing it to a detached child. Integration
+// tests set it for determinism; it also serves as an escape hatch when the
+// detached child is undesirable (e.g. debugging).
+const envSessionEndSyncCondense = "ENTIRE_SESSION_END_SYNC"
+
+// sessionEndCondenseSpawn is the process-spawn seam used by
+// handleLifecycleSessionEnd. Swapped in tests so they can assert the hook
+// requests a detached condense without forking a real subprocess (a real
+// `go test` binary doesn't understand `__condense_session` as an argument).
+// Production code always uses spawnDetachedSessionEndCondense.
+var sessionEndCondenseSpawn = spawnDetachedSessionEndCondense
+
+// spawnDetachedSessionEndCondense starts `entire __condense_session <id>` as
+// a detached child so the eager condense survives the SessionEnd hook being
+// cancelled (agents give these hooks a short budget — Claude Code cancels
+// after ~1.5s — and never wait for them on exit). The child runs from the
+// worktree root because the strategy resolves the repo and session store
+// from its working directory.
+func spawnDetachedSessionEndCondense(worktreeRoot, sessionID string) {
+	execx.SpawnDetached(worktreeRoot, "__condense_session", sessionID)
+}
+
+// newCondenseSessionCmd creates the hidden command that runs the eager
+// session-end condense out of band. It is invoked by
+// spawnDetachedSessionEndCondense from a detached subprocess and should not
+// be called directly.
+func newCondenseSessionCmd() *cobra.Command {
+	return &cobra.Command{
+		Use:    "__condense_session <session-id>",
+		Hidden: true,
+		Args:   cobra.ExactArgs(1),
+		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
+			ctx := cmd.Context()
+			// Detached child with discarded stdout/stderr: initialize file
+			// logging so a failing condense is diagnosable in
+			// .entire/logs/entire.log rather than vanishing. Guard on
+			// WorktreeRoot first — matching __refresh_trail_enablement — so a
+			// child whose worktree was removed between spawn and exec doesn't
+			// create a stray .entire/logs/ in an arbitrary directory.
+			if _, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx); err == nil {
+				logging.SetLogLevelGetter(GetLogLevel)
+				if err := logging.Init(ctx, ""); err == nil {
+					defer logging.Close()
+				}
+			}
+			sessionID := args[0]
+			if err := GetStrategy(ctx).CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed(ctx, sessionID); err != nil {
+				// Fail-open, like the inline condense it replaces: PostCommit
+				// retries on the next commit and the exited-session sweep
+				// retries from status/doctor.
+				logging.Warn(logging.WithComponent(ctx, "lifecycle"),
+					"detached session-end condense failed",
+					slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
+					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
+			}
+			return nil
+		},
+	}
+}

+

+
+// swapSessionEndCondenseSpawn replaces the detached-condense spawn seam with a
+// recorder and restores it on cleanup. Tests using it must not run in parallel
+// (package-level seam).
+func swapSessionEndCondenseSpawn(t *testing.T) *[]string {
+	t.Helper()
+	var spawned []string
+	orig := sessionEndCondenseSpawn
+	sessionEndCondenseSpawn = func(_, sessionID string) {
+		spawned = append(spawned, sessionID)
+	}
+	t.Cleanup(func() { sessionEndCondenseSpawn = orig })
+	return &spawned
+}

+	t.Helper()

+		StartedAt:  time.Now(),
+		Phase:      session.PhaseIdle,

+// it inline.

+	dir := setupGitRepoForPhaseTest(t)

+
+	const sessionID = "test-session-end-detach"
+	saveIdleSessionForEndTest(t, sessionID)
+	spawned := swapSessionEndCondenseSpawn(t)
+
+	event := &agent.Event{Type: agent.SessionEnd, SessionID: sessionID}
+	require.NoError(t, handleLifecycleSessionEnd(context.Background(), newMockAgent(), event))
+
+	loaded, err := strategy.LoadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotNil(t, loaded)
+	assert.Equal(t, session.PhaseEnded, loaded.Phase,
+		"session must be marked ENDED synchronously")
+	assert.False(t, loaded.FullyCondensed,
+		"condense must not run inline on the hook path")
+	assert.Equal(t, []string{sessionID}, *spawned,
+		"exactly one detached condense must be requested for the ended session")
+}
+
+// TestHandleLifecycleSessionEnd_SyncEnvCondensesInline verifies the
+// ENTIRE_SESSION_END_SYNC escape hatch keeps the pre-detach synchronous
+// behavior (used by integration tests for determinism).
+func TestHandleLifecycleSessionEnd_SyncEnvCondensesInline(t *testing.T) {
+	dir := setupGitRepoForPhaseTest(t)
+	t.Chdir(dir)
+	t.Setenv(envSessionEndSyncCondense, "1")
+
+	const sessionID = "test-session-end-sync"
+	saveIdleSessionForEndTest(t, sessionID)
+	spawned := swapSessionEndCondenseSpawn(t)
+
+	event := &agent.Event{Type: agent.SessionEnd, SessionID: sessionID}

+
+	loaded, err := strategy.LoadSessionState(context.Background(), sessionID)
+	require.NoError(t, err)
+	require.NotNil(t, loaded)

+
+// TestHandleLifecycleSessionEnd_NoSpawnWhenSessionMissing verifies no detached
+// child is forked when there is no session to condense.
+func TestHandleLifecycleSessionEnd_NoSpawnWhenSessionMissing(t *testing.T) {
+	dir := setupGitRepoForPhaseTest(t)
+	t.Chdir(dir)
+
+	spawned := swapSessionEndCondenseSpawn(t)
+
+	event := &agent.Event{Type: agent.SessionEnd, SessionID: "no-such-session"}
+	require.NoError(t, handleLifecycleSessionEnd(context.Background(), newMockAgent(), event))

+
+// TestCondenseSessionCmd_MarksFullyCondensed verifies the hidden
+// __condense_session command runs the eager condense for an ended session.
+func TestCondenseSessionCmd_MarksFullyCondensed(t *testing.T) {
+	dir := setupGitRepoForPhaseTest(t)
+	t.Chdir(dir)
+
+	const sessionID = "test-condense-session-cmd"
+	now := time.Now()
+	state := &strategy.SessionState{
+		SessionID:  sessionID,
+		BaseCommit: "abc123",

+
+// TestCondenseSessionCmd_MissingSessionIsFailOpen verifies the detached child
+// never errors on a session that disappeared between spawn and exec.
+func TestCondenseSessionCmd_MissingSessionIsFailOpen(t *testing.T) {

+	t.Chdir(dir)
+
+	cmd := newCondenseSessionCmd()

+//go:build integration
+
+package integration
+
+import (
+	"testing"
+	"time"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/session"
+)
+
+// TestSessionEnd_DetachedCondense exercises the production SessionEnd flow:
+// the hook marks the session ENDED inline (fast enough for agents' short
+// SessionEnd budgets — Claude Code cancels the hook after ~1.5s) and hands
+// the eager condense to a detached __condense_session child that survives
+// the hook process being killed. The ENDED mark must be observable as soon
+// as the hook returns; the condense lands asynchronously.
+func TestSessionEnd_DetachedCondense(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
+	sess := env.NewSession()
+
+	if err := env.SimulateUserPromptSubmit(sess.ID); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("SimulateUserPromptSubmit failed: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	env.WriteFile("detached.go", "package main\n\nfunc Detached() {}\n")
+	sess.CreateTranscript("Create detached.go", []FileChange{
+		{Path: "detached.go", Content: "package main\n\nfunc Detached() {}\n"},
+	})
+
+	// Commit the file BEFORE stopping so FilesTouched is empty at session end
+	// and the eager condense actually runs (sessions with FilesTouched defer
+	// to PostCommit for carry-forward tracking).
+	env.GitAdd("detached.go")
+	env.GitCommitWithShadowHooks("Add detached.go", "detached.go")
+
+	if err := env.SimulateStop(sess.ID, sess.TranscriptPath); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("SimulateStop failed: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	if err := env.SimulateSessionEndDetached(sess.ID); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("SimulateSessionEndDetached failed: %v", err)
+	}
+
+	// The ENDED mark is synchronous — it must hold the moment the hook returns.
+	state, err := env.GetSessionState(sess.ID)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("GetSessionState failed: %v", err)
+	}
+	if state == nil {
+		t.Fatal("session state missing after session-end")
+	}
+	if state.Phase != session.PhaseEnded {
+		t.Fatalf("phase = %s immediately after session-end, want ended", state.Phase)
+	}
+	if state.EndedAt == nil {
+		t.Fatal("EndedAt should be set immediately after session-end")
+	}
+
+	// The condense is detached — poll until the child lands it.
+	deadline := time.Now().Add(15 * time.Second)
+	for {
+		state, err = env.GetSessionState(sess.ID)
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("GetSessionState failed while polling: %v", err)
+		}
+		if state != nil && state.FullyCondensed {
+			break
+		}
+		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
+			t.Fatalf("detached condense did not mark session FullyCondensed within 15s (phase=%s)", state.Phase)
+		}
+		time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
+	}
+}

+package cli
+
+import (
+	"log/slog"
+
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/execx"
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/logging"
+	"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
+
+	"github.com/spf13/cobra"
+)
+
+// envSessionEndSyncCondense forces the SessionEnd hook to run the eager
+// condense inline instead of handing it to a detached child. Integration
+// tests set it for determinism; it also serves as an escape hatch when the
+// detached child is undesirable (e.g. debugging).
+const envSessionEndSyncCondense = "ENTIRE_SESSION_END_SYNC"
+
+// sessionEndCondenseSpawn is the process-spawn seam used by
+// handleLifecycleSessionEnd. Swapped in tests so they can assert the hook
+// requests a detached condense without forking a real subprocess (a real
+// `go test` binary doesn't understand `__condense_session` as an argument).
+// Production code always uses spawnDetachedSessionEndCondense.
+var sessionEndCondenseSpawn = spawnDetachedSessionEndCondense
+
+// spawnDetachedSessionEndCondense starts `entire __condense_session <id>` as
+// a detached child so the eager condense survives the SessionEnd hook being
+// cancelled (agents give these hooks a short budget — Claude Code cancels
+// after ~1.5s — and never wait for them on exit). The child runs from the
+// worktree root because the strategy resolves the repo and session store
+// from its working directory.
+func spawnDetachedSessionEndCondense(worktreeRoot, sessionID string) {
+	execx.SpawnDetached(worktreeRoot, "__condense_session", sessionID)
+}
+
+// newCondenseSessionCmd creates the hidden command that runs the eager
+// session-end condense out of band. It is invoked by
+// spawnDetachedSessionEndCondense from a detached subprocess and should not
+// be called directly.
+func newCondenseSessionCmd() *cobra.Command {
+	return &cobra.Command{
+		Use:    "__condense_session <session-id>",
+		Hidden: true,
+		Args:   cobra.ExactArgs(1),
+		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
+			ctx := cmd.Context()
+			// Detached child with discarded stdout/stderr: initialize file
+			// logging so a failing condense is diagnosable in
+			// .entire/logs/entire.log rather than vanishing. Guard on
+			// WorktreeRoot first — matching __refresh_trail_enablement — so a
+			// child whose worktree was removed between spawn and exec doesn't
+			// create a stray .entire/logs/ in an arbitrary directory.
+			if _, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx); err == nil {
+				logging.SetLogLevelGetter(GetLogLevel)
+				if err := logging.Init(ctx, ""); err == nil {
+					defer logging.Close()
+				}
+			}
+			sessionID := args[0]
+			if err := GetStrategy(ctx).CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed(ctx, sessionID); err != nil {
+				// Fail-open, like the inline condense it replaces: PostCommit
+				// retries on the next commit and the exited-session sweep
+				// retries from status/doctor.
+				logging.Warn(logging.WithComponent(ctx, "lifecycle"),
+					"detached session-end condense failed",
+					slog.String("session_id", sessionID),
+					slog.String("error", err.Error()))
+			}
+			return nil
+		},
+	}
+}

content.text:
# Comprehensive PR Review

Run a comprehensive pull request review using multiple specialized agents, each focusing on a different aspect of code quality.

**Review Aspects (optional):** "1844"

## Review Workflow:

1. **Determine Review Scope**
   - Check git status to identify changed files
   - Parse arguments to see if user requested specific review aspects
   - Default: Run all applicable reviews

2. **Available Review Aspects:**

   - **comments** - Analyze code comment accuracy and maintainability
   - **tests** - Review test coverage quality and completeness
   - **errors** - Check error handling for silent failures
   - **types** - Analyze type design and invariants (if new types added)
   - **code** - General code review for project guidelines
   - **simplify** - Simplify code for clarity and maintainability
   - **all** - Run all applicable reviews (default)

3. **Identify Changed Files**
   - Run `git diff --name-only` to see modified files
   - Check if PR already exists: `gh pr view`
   - Identify file types and what reviews apply

4. **Determine Applicable Reviews**

   Based on changes:
   - **Always applicable**: code-reviewer (general quality)
   - **If test files changed**: pr-test-analyzer
   - **If comments/docs added**: comment-analyzer
   - **If error handling changed**: silent-failure-hunter
   - **If types added/modified**: type-design-analyzer
   - **After passing review**: code-simplifier (polish and refine)

5. **Launch Review Agents**

   **Sequential approach** (one at a time):
   - Easier to understand and act on
   - Each report is complete before next
   - Good for interactive review

   **Parallel approach** (user can request):
   - Launch all agents simultaneously
   - Faster for comprehensive review
   - Results come back together

6. **Aggregate Results**

   After agents complete, summarize:
   - **Critical Issues** (must fix before merge)
   - **Important Issues** (should fix)
   - **Suggestions** (nice to have)
   - **Positive Observations** (what's good)

7. **Provide Action Plan**

   Organize findings:
   ```markdown
   # PR Review Summary

   ## Critical Issues (X found)
   - [agent-name]: Issue description [file:line]
   ```

## Summary

Reviewed the diff for PR #1844 (SessionEnd hook cancellation fix): the `scripts/entire-dev` build-cache change, the split of `handleLifecycleSessionEnd` into an inline ENDED mark + detached `__condense_session` child, the new `session_end_condense.go`, the `ENTIRE_SESSION_END_SYNC` escape hatch, and the associated unit + integration tests.

**Overall this is a clean, well-reasoned PR.** The concurrency design is sound: the detached child and racing PostCommit both serialize on the per-session `MutateSessionState` lock, and `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` re-loads state and re-checks `FilesTouched`/`StepCount` under that lock, so double-condense is a no-op rather than corruption. Privacy-safe logging (only IDs/paths/errors), correct repo-root-as-cwd for the detached child, fail-open error handling, and `logging.Warn`-before-`Init` verified safe (falls back to `slog.Default()` → discarded stderr). The `exec.Cmd` env-dedup trick in `SimulateSessionEndDetached` is correct (Go keeps the last value per key, and `GitIsolatedEnv()` includes `os.Environ()`), and the real-binary detached path is genuinely exercised because `testing.Testing()` is false in the spawned hook subprocess.

**I found no critical (≥90) must-fix bugs.** The items below are nice-to-have.

## Findings (ranked)

### 1. Detached condense doesn't re-verify phase is still ENDED (nice-to-have, confidence ~80)
`cmd/entire/cli/session_end_condense.go:59-68` → `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` (`strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:1303`)

The detached child calls `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` unconditionally; it never re-checks that the session is still `PhaseEnded`. Between the inline `markSessionEnded` and the child acquiring the lock there is now a real (previously ~zero) time window. If the same session ID were reactivated in that window, the child could set `FullyCondensed=true` and reset the checkpoint window mid-session. In practice the risk is low: Claude Code session IDs are terminal at SessionEnd (resume mints a new ID), `FilesTouched>0` sessions are skipped (deferred to PostCommit), and the inline path (`endSessionNow`) had the same no-phase-guard behavior — the detach only widens the window. Compare with `finalizeExitedSessions` (`session_finalize.go:37`), which passes a guard closure to `markSessionEnded` precisely to re-validate under the lock. Consider whether the condense should bail if the reloaded state is no longer ENDED. Largely pre-existing; flagging because the PR widens the window.

### 2. CLAUDE.md hidden-infrastructure-commands list not updated (nice-to-have, confidence ~75)
`CLAUDE.md:134-135`

The new hidden `__condense_session` command is not added to the documented "Hidden infrastructure commands" list. CLAUDE.md explicitly asks to keep the file current. (Note the list is already non-exhaustive — `__refresh_trail_enablement` is also absent — so this is a soft convention, not a hard violation.) The command is otherwise correctly wired: hidden, excluded from checkpoint-policy warnings (`checkpoint_policy_warning.go`), and absent from `agent-help` (no `agentHelpAnnotation`).

### 3. Detached child in integration test may outlive the test → cleanup race (nice-to-have, confidence ~70)
`cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/session_end_detached_test.go:60-76`

The test polls until `FullyCondensed` is observed, but `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` runs `cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused` (`manual_commit_condensation.go:1385`) — including a `DeleteBranchCLI` git invocation — *after* setting `FullyCondensed` inside the mutation. So the test can observe completion and return while the detached child is still running `git` against the temp repo, racing `t.TempDir()` cleanup. Fail-open makes this harmless to correctness, but it's a potential source of flakiness / orphaned processes in CI. Worth polling on a signal that lands after cleanup, or accepting the residual git error.

### 4. `entire-dev` concurrent build-then-exec race (nice-to-have, confidence ~50; dev-only)
`scripts/entire-dev:49-54`

The comment acknowledges the rebuild race and the fallback covers a *failed* build. The residual concern is `exec "$bin"` racing a concurrent `go build -o "$bin"`: on Linux this is safe if `go build` renames into place (running inode kept), and a truncate-in-place would yield ETXTBSY to the writer → fallback. Either way it's handled, and this is local-dev tooling only, so impact is minimal. No change needed; noting for completeness since the task asked about rebuild races.

## Non-issues verified (in case they come up)
- **PostCommit vs detached condense race** — serialized by the per-session `MutateSessionState` lock; second condense is a no-op via `StepCount`/`FullyCondensed` checks. Fine.
- **Duplicate SessionEnd → double spawn** — `markSessionEnded` sets `ended=true` unconditionally (`lifecycle.go:1316`), so a repeated SessionEnd would spawn a second child, but it's a no-op. Pre-existing behavior; not worth fixing.
- **Detached child survives hook kill** — `execx.SpawnDetached` uses `context.Background()`, `Setsid`, and `Process.Release()`; correct for surviving the ~1.5s cancel.
- **Env/config isolation of the detached child** — inherits the fully-isolated env from the hook subprocess; correct.
- **Sync-branch worktreeRoot computed-but-unused** — compiles fine (used in the other branch); harmless.

# Test Coverage Review — PR #1844 (SessionEnd hook split: inline ENDED mark + detached condense)

The seam is justified, not a testing shortcut: `execx.SpawnDetached` is a hard no-op under `testing.Testing()` (`cmd/entire/cli/execx/spawn_detached.go:23`).

The three asked-about gaps score differently: the **reactivation race is real, unguarded, and untested**; the **rootErr sync fallback is untested but near-dead code**; the **launcher script — the actual root cause of the outage this PR fixes — has zero tests**. The 15s polling test is unlikely to flake.

## Ranked Gaps

### 1. Detached child condenses a reactivated session — unguarded and untested (criticality 7)

`CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` (`cmd/entire/cli/strategy/manual_commit_condensation.go:1288`) has **no phase guard**. The state machine explicitly allows revival: ENDED + `EventSessionStart` → IDLE, ENDED + `EventTurnStart` → ACTIVE (`cmd/entire/cli/session/phase.go:235-263`). If a session is resumed between `sessionEndCondenseSpawn` and the child's mutation, the child condenses a **live** session: `resetCheckpointWindow`, `PromptAttributions = nil`, `PendingPromptAttribution = nil`, `FullyCondensed = true` (lines 1361-1368) — wiping the revived session's in-flight attribution and moving `CheckpointTranscriptStart` mid-turn. This race existed inline (mark and condense are separate lock acquisitions), but the detach widens the window from microseconds to spawn latency, and on a loaded machine that's unbounded.

- **Failure it would catch:** resume a session immediately after exit → attribution data for the first revived turn silently lost; checkpoint window corrupted.

# PR #1844 Review Summary (4 agents + my own pass)

## Critical — fix before merge (2)

1. **Missing phase guard in the detached condense** — *flagged independently by 3 reviewers.* `CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed` never re-checks the session is still ENDED. The state machine explicitly allows revival (ENDED → ACTIVE on turn-start), and the detach widens the mark→condense window from microseconds to unbounded spawn latency. A session resumed in that window gets its **in-flight prompt attribution wiped and checkpoint window reset mid-turn** (`manual_commit_condensation.go:1361-1368`). Fix: skip inside the mutation (under the lock) when `Phase != PhaseEnded`, plus a unit test that currently fails.

2. **The launcher's "never blocks" contract has a hole** — *converged on by 2 reviewers.* If hook A `exec`s the cached binary while hook B's concurrent `go build` is rewriting it in place (go's output install isn't atomic across filesystems), A's `exec` fails and under `set -eu` the shell **aborts without reaching the PATH-binary fallback** — a non-zero hook exit, exactly what the script promises never happens. Fix: invoke the binary without `exec` and fall through to the fallback on exit 126/127 (keeps the up-to-date fast path that `mv -f`-style atomic swaps would sacrifice).

## Important — should fix (4)

3. **Silent spawn failure leaves zero evidence** (silent-failure, HIGH): if `SpawnDetached` fails (deleted cache binary via `entire clean`, ENOENT, fork exhaustion), the session is ENDED, the condense never runs, and *nothing* is logged — the old inline path at least warned. Fix: log the handoff at Info + surface `Start()` errors for a Warn.
4. **False safety-net comment**: `__condense_session` claims "the exited-session sweep retries" — it can't; the sweep is ACTIVE-only (the blind spot we found ourselves). The real retry surfaces are PostCommit and doctor. Comment must be corrected — it's the documented justification for fail-open.
5. **`~1.5s` hard-coded in four files** with no provenance — state it once (in `session_end_condense.go`, hedged "empirically, as of Claude Code 2.1.x, 2026-07"), reference it elsewhere.
6. **`entire-dev` misattributes all failures to "project isn't compiling"** and destroys compiler stderr — redirect build errors to `.entire/tmp/entire-dev-build.log` and name it in the fallback message.

## Suggestions (7)

- Rewrite the now-misleading "lockstep" comment on `endSessionNow`; document why the sweep still condenses inline
- Extend `TestShouldCheckCheckpointPolicyWarning` with `__condense_session` (pins the exclusion)
- Integration test: assert a real checkpoint landed (currently no test exercises the child doing *actual* tree-building condensation); nil-guard the poll's timeout `Fatalf`
- Unit test for the `rootErr` sync fallback; seam should record `worktreeRoot` too
- Fix the spawn-seam rationale comment (the no-fork safety is `testing.Testing()`, not the seam) and the stale "Used by" comment on `runHookInRepoDirWithExtraEnv`
- Add `__condense_session` to CLAUDE.md's hidden-commands list
- Launcher shell-script test suite (5 cases incl. the "never blocks" guarantee) — worthwhile but the biggest lift; candidate for follow-up

## Strengths (unanimous)

Concurrency design is sound (PostCommit vs child serialize on the per-session lock — verified, not assumed); tests are behavioral, not tautological; the seam pattern, fail-open + logged-Warn semantics, env-dedup trick, and child logging-init all verified correct; 15s polling test judged low flake risk; the retry lattice (PostCommit + doctor) genuinely exists.

## Recommended action

Fix 1–6 plus the cheap comment/test suggestions as one "address review findings" commit on the PR branch (the phase guard is the only one touching strategy code); park the launcher test suite as a follow-up. Want me to apply them?

// TestCondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed_Guards verifies the two early-exit conditions
// in CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed: sessions with no data are marked FullyCondensed
// immediately, and sessions with FilesTouched are left untouched for PostCommit.
func TestCondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed_Guards(t *testing.T) {
	t.Run("no data marks FullyCondensed immediately", func(t *testing.T) {
		dir := setupGitRepo(t)
		t.Chdir(dir)

		s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
		require.NoError(t, s.InitializeSession(context.Background(), "test-session", "Claude Code", "", "", ""))

		state, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), "test-session")
		require.NoError(t, err)
		now := time.Now()
		state.Phase = session.PhaseEnded
		state.EndedAt = &now
		state.StepCount = 0
		state.FilesTouched = nil
		require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(context.Background(), state))

		require.NoError(t, s.CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed(context.Background(), "test-session"))

		state, err = s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), "test-session")
		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.NotNil(t, state)
		assert.True(t, state.FullyCondensed)
		assert.Equal(t, session.PhaseEnded, state.Phase)
	})

	t.Run("with FilesTouched is a no-op", func(t *testing.T) {
		dir := setupGitRepo(t)
		t.Chdir(dir)

		s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
		require.NoError(t, s.InitializeSession(context.Background(), "test-session", "Claude Code", "", "", ""))

		state, err := s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), "test-session")
		require.NoError(t, err)
		now := time.Now()
		state.Phase = session.PhaseEnded
		state.EndedAt = &now
		state.FilesTouched = []string{"some_file.txt"}
		require.NoError(t, s.saveSessionState(context.Background(), state))

		require.NoError(t, s.CondenseAndMarkFullyCondensed(context.Background(), "test-session"))

		state, err = s.loadSessionState(context.Background(), "test-session")
		require.NoError(t, err)
		require.NotNil(t, state)
		assert.False(t, state.FullyCondensed)
		assert.Equal(t, []string{"some_file.txt"}, state.FilesTouched)
	})
}

#!/bin/sh
# Entire CLI local-development hook launcher.
#
# In local-dev mode, Entire hooks invoke the CLI built straight from source.
# The binary is cached under .entire/tmp/ (ignored via the committed
# .entire/.gitignore) and "go build" only relinks it when the source changed,
# so an up-to-date tree costs one staleness check instead of a full link.
# This matters for hooks with a tight deadline — agents cancel SessionEnd
# hooks after a short (~1-2s) budget (see spawnDetachedSessionEndCondense in
# cmd/entire/cli/session_end_condense.go), which the previous
# probe-then-"go run" flow (two full links per invocation) could not meet.
#
# When the tree does not compile (for example while an agent is resolving a
# merge conflict) the build fails and this launcher falls back to an "entire"
# binary on PATH. If neither is available it exits 0 so it never blocks the
# surrounding git or agent operation.
#
# Usage: scripts/entire-dev <entire args...>
#
# All local-dev hooks delegate here so the build-and-fallback logic lives in
# one place rather than being duplicated across generated hook commands.

set -eu

# Informational messages go to stderr so they never pollute hook stdout (some
# hooks emit JSON there).
log() {
	printf '[entire-dev] %s\n' "$1" >&2
}

# Resolve the repository root from this script's own location so it works
# regardless of the caller's working directory. Parameter expansion avoids
# depending on external tools like dirname, which may not be on PATH when this
# runs from a minimal hook environment.
case "$0" in
	*/*) script_dir=${0%/*} ;;
	*) script_dir=. ;;
esac
root=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$script_dir/.." && pwd)
# Build the whole cmd/entire package, not just main.go: package main is
# split across multiple files (e.g. the git-remote-entire dispatch in
# remotehelper.go), and naming a single file would leave the others out and
# fail to compile.
pkg="$root/cmd/entire"

# Build (incrementally) into the per-worktree cache and run the result.
# "entire clean" may remove .entire/tmp/, which just costs one rebuild.
# Build stderr goes to a log file, not the hook's stderr: compiler spew would
# pollute agent-visible output, but discarding it entirely would leave
# "build failed" undiagnosable.
bin="$root/.entire/tmp/entire-dev-bin"
buildlog="$root/.entire/tmp/entire-dev-build.log"
if ! command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	log "go not found on PATH; falling back"
elif ! mkdir -p "${bin%/*}" 2>/dev/null; then
	log "cannot create ${bin%/*}; falling back"
elif ! go build -o "$bin" "$pkg" >/dev/null 2>"$buildlog"; then
	log "go build failed (details: .entire/tmp/entire-dev-build.log); falling back"
else
	# Run without exec: a concurrent invocation can be rewriting $bin (go's
	# output install is not atomic on every filesystem), and a failed exec
	# would abort this shell without reaching the fallbacks below, breaking
	# the never-block contract. Launch failures surface as 126/127; anything
	# else is the CLI's own exit status and is passed through.
	status=0
	"$bin" "$@" || status=$?
	if [ "$status" -ne 126 ] && [ "$status" -ne 127 ]; then
		exit "$status"
	fi
	log "cached binary failed to launch (status $status, concurrent rebuild?); falling back"
fi

# The tree does not build (or the cached binary couldn't run): fall back to
# the installed binary so hooks keep working while the source is broken.
if command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	log "using the entire binary on PATH ($(command -v entire))"
	exec entire "$@"
fi

# Nothing to run: do not block the surrounding operation.
log "no runnable entire binary; skipping hook"
exit 0

# Build (incrementally) into the per-worktree cache and run the result.
# "entire clean" may remove .entire/tmp/, which just costs one rebuild.
# Build stderr goes to a log file, not the hook's stderr: compiler spew would
# pollute agent-visible output, but discarding it entirely would leave
# "build failed" undiagnosable.
bin="$root/.entire/tmp/entire-dev-bin"
buildlog="$root/.entire/tmp/entire-dev-build.log"
if ! command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	log "go not found on PATH; falling back"
elif ! mkdir -p "${bin%/*}" 2>/dev/null; then
	log "cannot create ${bin%/*}; falling back"
elif ! go build -o "$bin" "$pkg" >/dev/null 2>"$buildlog"; then
	log "go build failed (details: .entire/tmp/entire-dev-build.log); falling back"
else
	# Run without exec: a concurrent invocation can be rewriting $bin (go's
	# output install is not atomic on every filesystem), and a failed exec
	# would abort this shell without reaching the fallbacks below, breaking
	# the never-block contract. Launch failures surface as 126/127; anything
	# else is the CLI's own exit status and is passed through.
	status=0
	"$bin" "$@" || status=$?
	if [ "$status" -ne 126 ] && [ "$status" -ne 127 ]; then
		exit "$status"
	fi
	log "cached binary failed to launch (status $status, concurrent rebuild?); falling back"
fi

# The tree does not build (or the cached binary couldn't run): fall back to
# the installed binary so hooks keep working while the source is broken.
if command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	log "using the entire binary on PATH ($(command -v entire))"
	exec entire "$@"
fi

# Nothing to run: do not block the surrounding operation.
log "no runnable entire binary; skipping hook"
exit 0

#!/bin/sh
# Entire CLI local-development hook launcher.
#
# In local-dev mode, Entire hooks invoke the CLI built straight from source.
# The binary is cached under .entire/tmp/ (ignored via the committed
# .entire/.gitignore) and "go build" only relinks it when the source changed,
# so an up-to-date tree costs one staleness check instead of a full link.
# This matters for hooks with a tight deadline — agents cancel SessionEnd
# hooks after a short (~1-2s) budget (see spawnDetachedSessionEndCondense in
# cmd/entire/cli/session_end_condense.go), which the previous

#!/bin/sh
# Entire CLI local-development hook launcher.
#
# In local-dev mode, Entire hooks invoke the CLI built straight from source.
# The binary is cached under .entire/tmp/ (ignored via the committed
# .entire/.gitignore) and "go build" only relinks it when the source changed,
# so an up-to-date tree costs one staleness check instead of a full link.
# This matters for hooks with a tight deadline — agents cancel SessionEnd
# hooks after a short (~1-2s) budget (see spawnDetachedSessionEndCondense in
# cmd/entire/cli/session_end_condense.go), which the previous
# probe-then-"go run" flow (two full links per invocation) could not meet.
#
# When the tree does not compile (for example while an agent is resolving a
# merge conflict) the build fails and this launcher falls back to an "entire"
# binary on PATH. If neither is available it exits 0 so it never blocks the
# surrounding git or agent operation.
#
# Usage: scripts/entire-dev <entire args...>
#
# All local-dev hooks delegate here so the build-and-fallback logic lives in
# one place rather than being duplicated across generated hook commands.

set -eu

# Informational messages go to stderr so they never pollute hook stdout (some
# hooks emit JSON there).
log() {
	printf '[entire-dev] %s\n' "$1" >&2
}

# Resolve the repository root from this script's own location so it works
# regardless of the caller's working directory. Parameter expansion avoids
# depending on external tools like dirname, which may not be on PATH when this
# runs from a minimal hook environment.
case "$0" in
	*/*) script_dir=${0%/*} ;;
	*) script_dir=. ;;
esac
root=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$script_dir/.." && pwd)
# Build the whole cmd/entire package, not just main.go: package main is
# split across multiple files (e.g. the git-remote-entire dispatch in
# remotehelper.go), and naming a single file would leave the others out and
# fail to compile. The path is relative and paired with "go build -C $root":
# an absolute package path would be resolved against the *caller's* module
# (go interprets directory arguments relative to the current module), which
# breaks when the hook is invoked from outside this repo.
pkg="./cmd/entire"

# Build (incrementally) into the per-worktree cache and run the result.
# "entire clean" may remove .entire/tmp/, which just costs one rebuild.
# Build stderr goes to a log file, not the hook's stderr: compiler spew would
# pollute agent-visible output, but discarding it entirely would leave
# "build failed" undiagnosable.
bin="$root/.entire/tmp/entire-dev-bin"
if command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	# mkdir may be absent from a minimal hook PATH; if the cache dir can't be
	# created, go build fails to write its output and we fall back below.
	mkdir -p "${bin%/*}" 2>/dev/null || true
	buildlog="${bin%/*}/entire-dev-build.log"
	[ -d "${bin%/*}" ] || buildlog=/dev/null
	if go build -C "$root" -o "$bin" "$pkg" >/dev/null 2>"$buildlog"; then
		# Run without exec: a concurrent invocation can be rewriting $bin
		# (go's output install is not atomic on every filesystem), and a
		# failed exec would abort this shell without reaching the fallbacks
		# below, breaking the never-block contract. Launch failures surface
		# as 126/127; anything else is the CLI's own exit status and is
		# passed through.
		status=0
		"$bin" "$@" || status=$?
		if [ "$status" -ne 126 ] && [ "$status" -ne 127 ]; then
			exit "$status"
		fi
		log "cached binary failed to launch (status $status, concurrent rebuild?)"
	else
		log "go build failed (details: $buildlog)"
	fi
else
	log "go not found on PATH"
fi

# The tree does not build (or the cached binary couldn't run): fall back to
# the installed binary so hooks keep working while the source is broken.
if command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then
	log "falling back to the entire binary on PATH ($(command -v entire))"
	exec entire "$@"
fi

# Nothing to run: do not block the surrounding operation.
log "no entire binary on PATH; skipping hook"
exit 0
